title: Relative flatness extends finite presentation from a dense open
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], let $\mathcal F$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module flat over $S$, and let $U\subset S$ be an open subscheme. Assume $U$ is retrocompact, meaning that its intersection with every quasi-compact open of $S$ is quasi-compact, and scheme-theoretically dense, meaning $\mathcal O_S\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective for $j:U\hookrightarrow S$. If $\mathcal F|_{f^{-1}(U)}$ is of finite presentation, then $\mathcal F$ is of finite presentation. Finite type, finite presentation and relative flatness are as in [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over].

proof.text: Finite presentation is local on X and S, so work on affine opens X=Spec(B), S=Spec(A), with B finitely presented over A and the quasi-coherent finite-type module represented by a finite B-module N. Retrocompactness makes U∩Spec(A) quasi-compact, hence U=D(f_1)∪⋯∪D(f_n) for elements f_i∈A. Scheme-theoretic density gives an injective map A→A_{f_1}×⋯×A_{f_n}.

source.place: Tag 081N proof, affine reduction and first paragraph.

proof.text: Fix a prime q of B. Choose a finite free surjection B^m→N. Since N is the filtered colimit of quotients B^m/(k_1,…,k_t) by finite subsets of its kernel, the stalk lemma of Tag 05I7 (the node lem-trf-flat-finite-type-flat-point-local) first gives that N_q is finitely presented over B_q because N_q is flat over A. Choose a finite quotient N′ and a surjection N′→N which is an isomorphism after each localization at f_i and at q. The q-local equality uses finite presentation of N_q, while the other equalities are witnessed after multiplying by powers of the inverted elements. Consequently N′_q≅N_q is flat over A.

source.place: Tag 081N proof, filtered-colimit paragraph choosing k_1,…,k_t, using Tag 05I7.

proof.text: The finite free presentation of N′ by finitely many relations makes N′ a finitely presented B-module. Apply the existing openness-of-flatness node lem-weil-pbc-openness-of-flatness, which is Tag 00RC, to A→B and N′ at q. Since N′_q is A-flat, its flat locus is open, so there exists g∉q such that N′_g is flat over A.

source.place: Tag 081N proof, paragraph invoking Algebra, Theorem 00RC after the finite-relation approximation.

proof.text: In the localization comparison diagram, the bottom map ∏_i N′_{gf_i}→∏_i N_{gf_i} is an isomorphism by construction. Flatness of N′_g over A, together with the injective map A→∏_iA_{f_i}, makes the left vertical map injective by the defining tensor criterion for flatness; the top map is therefore injective, and it is surjective from N′→N. Hence N_g≅N′_g is finitely presented over B_g.

source.place: Tag 081N proof, displayed diagram and injectivity argument.

proof.text: As q was arbitrary, the elements g obtained above give a basic-open cover of Spec(B) on which N is finitely presented. Finite presentation of a quasi-coherent module is local on the source, so the original sheaf F is of finite presentation on X.

source.place: Tag 081N proof, final application of Algebra, Lemma cover.
